blocking_items.requirement: 0787 check 1: one guarded read per file per snapshot; A226 item 1 single-read rule.
blocking_items.finding: snapshot groups by realpath, not descriptor (dev, ino). Two hard-link paths to one regular file each call read_once, read the same inode twice, and return exit 0. OneRead.get has the same realpath-only cache for collect.
blocking_items.reproduction: OWN_CHECKS.json and own_checks_cx1.py: synthetic input.txt and alias.txt have equal dev/ino; each bytes_read=6; snapshot exit=0. No production input was mutated.
blocking_items.scope: A contract violation, not demonstrated acceptance of unhashed bytes. Both observations are hashed correctly; no scientific result is implicated.
blocking_items.requested_fix: Use file identity to share a single content-read result across aliases, while retaining each path resolution and checking descriptor identity safely; alternatively refuse duplicate inode aliases before a second content read. Add hard-link regressions for snapshot and collect, with independent content-read counts. Publish an immutable successor.

TESTED: All six dispatch hashes verified before and after.
82/82 published suite rerun, zero failures; 45/45 mutations killed with passing baseline.
Independent inert hard-link alias test reproduces CX1-ENV-01.
Independent synthetic NGC3198/result-name collect guard: zero payload opens; missing-file snapshot returns exit 3.
Source review: each individual read_once hashes/counts its own chunks and uses descriptor metadata; collect parses that buffer. D1-D7 mechanics reviewed against A228.

D1 exclusion matches realpath and inode; D2 default 0/reason for depth; D3 scope and recorded exclusions; D4 xattr/ctime classification; D5 parse/cap refusal; D6 both compare shas; D7 encoding refusal.
Compare checks byte/size/mtime/inode, mismatches, missing status and resolution changes; invalidation exit 3 and explicit refusals exit 2.
choices_assessment: Inode exclusion, exact-spelling scope, non-container scope refusal, depth reason, exclusion reasons, over-cap followed-document refusal and descriptor xattr-name reads are consistent with or conservatively implement the rulings.

Optional snapshot pins-sha256 is accepted only with documented root procedure always supplying it. Root must enforce C1 /tail_readiness scope and correct phase sources; tool does not infer C1 identity.

D4 is implemented as ruled. Endpoint snapshots do not prove continuous immutability: a transient modification restored before END, with mtime restored and changed xattr names, can be classified as explained metadata. This is a policy limitation, not an additional implementation blocker.
N6 parent-folder race remains disclosed; no additional real snapshot was taken.
